strengths: Novel and well-motivated approach using Fourier features grounded in interpretability findings (Zhou et al. 2024)
Solid mathematical foundation with rigorous lemmas justifying digit recovery via modular arithmetic
Comprehensive experimental methodology with extensive ablations on synthetic arithmetic tasks
Impressive quantitative results: 64× data efficiency, 3-6× token reduction, perfect accuracy on multiple benchmarks
Strong reproducibility with detailed algorithms, clear experimental setup, and thorough appendix
Evidence of real-model integration: continual pretraining on Llama-3.1 without harming semantics; FineWeb pretraining maintains/improves language modeling
Systematic evaluation across model sizes, data regimes, and architectural variations
weaknesses: Evaluation almost exclusively on synthetic arithmetic tasks; no assessment on standard quantitative reasoning benchmarks (MATH, GSM8K, DROP)
Real-world applicability unclear: continual pretraining on Llama shows modest improvements (4-digit addition: 51.35% → 59.00%), not transformative
Theoretical-practice gap: Lemma D.2 assumes orthogonality not guaranteed in practice; decoding uses approximate argmax without error characterization
Limited scope of synthetic evaluation: tasks restricted to 6 digits primarily (except 60-digit addition at 97.42% accuracy); no systematic out-of-distribution robustness analysis
Float64 precision limits (15 digits) inadequately addressed; chunking solution adds complexity and is only evaluated up to 60 digits
Incomplete baseline comparisons: XVAL achieves 0.44% on decimal addition (seems suspiciously low); limited comparison with recent methods; fine-tuned Llama comparison conflates model size and method
Design choice justifications incomplete: Why 2 dimensions per digit? Base-10 period choice justified primarily by prior empirical observations, not fundamental principles
No evaluation of robustness to malformed numbers, scientific notation, negative numbers, or real-world number distributions (violates uniform sampling assumptions)
Missing standard ablations: sensitivity to embedding dimension d, effect of non-power-of-10 periods, alternative decoding strategies
Weak evidence that improved arithmetic translates to better downstream task performance on real-world quantitative reasoning
